topic: Autoprompt Skill Review 2026: A Coding-Agent Skill That Cuts Failures by 45%

key_points: First-party project (MIT license, ~942 stars, created 2026-08-17).
Primary claim: 45% fewer failures on agentic coding tasks.
Measured OpenCode vs OpenCode+Autoprompt on Terminal-Bench 2.1: 60/89 to 73/89 solved, 67.42% to 82.02%, failures 29 to 16.
Explicitly states trade-off of ~3x time and ~2x tokens (as planning estimates, not measured).
Multi-agent orchestration layer: layers separate coordination, management, execution, and independent 'judge' judgment.
Invoked with a slash command like `/autoprompt` with a goal; handles scoping, implement, test, review, repair, verify.
Independent technical deep-dive; frames Autoprompt as an orchestration layer, not a prompt template.
Numbers come from the project's own docs (OpenCode 1.18.7, one benchmark, one run) and were not reproduced.
Cost side is weaker evidence: 3x time/2x tokens are planning estimates because token logs were not retained.
Judge is a separate model call with its own context so it does not inherit the builder's false confidence.
Practical guidance: cap concurrency with mode=custom max_subs=N on small VPS; watch RAM/CPU; requires Node 20+, Python 3.11+, Bash 4.3+.
Recommended for tasks you'd otherwise supervise for an hour; not for small known-file-to-edit changes or repos with no tests.
News brief treating the 45% figure as a vendor claim, not a settled fact.
437 stars in three days on GitHub (~153 stars/day), fast growth signals developer resonance.
Positions it in the 'agent-skill-as-plugin' reliability-patching category.
Recommendation: test it, but require independent measurement before standardizing.
Argues many agent failures come from bad prompts (misunderstood ask, skipped context, drift), which the skill hardens.
SEO-style review; cites 45% failure reduction and 67.42% to ~82% success jump.
Supports Codex (v0.147.0), OpenCode (v1.18.7), Prime Agent (v0.7.2), etc.
Install via npm or from source; claims simple reconfiguration.
Weak/unsupported claims (financial firm debug-time drops, e-commerce reliability) — lower-evidence source.
Repeats vendor numbers without independent verification.
Authoritative evidence boundary note from the repo.
Baseline OpenCode run has all 89 retained per-task verdicts.
Autoprompt score is a recorded completed aggregate; original per-task map was not retained, so cannot be rebuilt task-by-task.
DeepSeek's 82.7% used its own harness/settings — an external reference, NOT a comparable third run.
Both runs used DeepSeek V4 Flash, OpenCode 1.18.7, and the same 89 tasks.

stats.fact: On Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks, OpenCode 1.18.7, DeepSeek V4 Flash), failures fell from 29 to 16 with Autoprompt — 45% fewer.
Tasks solved rose from 60 of 89 (67.42%) to 73 of 89 (82.02%) — +13 solves, +14.61 points.
DeepSeek separately reported 82.7% on its own harness and settings — used as an external reference, not a comparable third run.
Autoprompt 1.0.0 published ~18 Aug 2026; 1.0.4 by 21 Aug 2026 (fast-moving); ~942 stars by late Sep 2026; 437 stars in first 3 days (~153/day).
Project states about 3x execution time and about 2x tokens as planning estimates from user reports; timing/token logs were not retained.
Supports 9 audited coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kilo Code, VS Code, Prime Agent, Oh My Pi, DeepSeek Harness, Reasonix.
Requirements: Node.js 20+, Python 3.11+ (exposed as `python` with PyYAML), Bash 4.3+ on macOS/Linux.

angles: The 45% claim is a single vendor-run benchmark — distinguish 'measured in one run' from 'reproducible'; no independent agent/codebase run published.
Why it works: separation of concerns — an independent judge (separate model call/context) that doesn't inherit the builder's false confidence; not just better prompting.
The real cost: you buy accuracy with 3x time and 2x tokens; weigh against budget caps (mode=tokensaver, mode=custom max_subs=N) on small machines.
When NOT to use it: small known-file edits, repos with no tests (judge can't run anything), low-memory VPS, near metered budget.
Category context: part of the fast-growing 'agent-skill-as-plugin' reliability layer, alongside behaviour skills (unlazy, ponytail, Old Coder) — pick the right tool.
Evidence-boundary honesty is a strength: the repo itself admits the Autoprompt aggregate cannot be rebuilt task-by-task.
Practical setup pitfalls on Ubuntu/Debian: `python` not found (use python-is-python3), EACCES npm global prefix.
